title: C405 — Inline connector reference
introduction:
This inline connection brings together lighting, rear parking-aid, release-switch and ground circuits. I start with the connector identity and harness heading before looking at individual wires. A familiar-looking housing is a useful clue, but the circuit map is what gives every connection its address.

Choose the MALE or FEMALE section, then pair its illustration with its own tables. The MALE drawing's labels decrease downward within each column; the FEMALE drawing's labels increase downward. Match a printed cavity label to the Cavity column, then read across for circuit identity, wire description, function and terminal listing. Gray-filled positions correspond to blank circuit assignments. Compare the faces by cavity and circuit identity rather than by their apparent position on the page.

Function wording retains its positional alternatives and equipment labels; it does not establish that every listed feature is fitted to your car. A relay label identifies an electrical role and does not guarantee a separate plug-in relay. The hardware tables are cross-references, while physical viewing direction, access, release, testing and repair require the matching procedure. Gauge conventions and the Size and Used codes remain undefined here; they are not a basis for choosing replacement wire.

edits.why: The gender and harness identity keep this illustration tied to the correct face record. I use that pairing before following any cavity into the circuit table.

The printed cavity label identifies the table row; Function then distinguishes the circuit's job. Preserve the alternative location descriptions and polarity marks rather than narrowing them to an unsupported interpretation.
This drawing has a different vertical numbering order and its own terminal listings. Shared circuit assignments across the connection do not make the hardware records interchangeable.

Read terminal information from this face's row even when the circuit identity matches the other face. The map describes the assigned connection; it does not show whether that connection can carry its working load.

Engineering Shell groups the listed pigtails with the corresponding face hardware, and Service Part names the service item. Where entries share a shell, this table alone does not resolve which kit a particular repair needs.
